explanation: The theorem's statement mentions `ModularForm.heckeDiagMatrix`, which does not exist in Mathlib at all (grep for `heckeDiagMatrix`/`heckeDiag` in the Mathlib tree returns nothing; Mathlib's `Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/*` has no Hecke operator/diagonal matrix definitions). Its mathematical content is that precomposition with the surjective map `τ ↦ heckeDiagMatrix p • τ` on the upper half plane preserves nonzeroness of a function; I searched Mathlib's `Logic/Function/Basic.lean` (`Injective.of_comp`, `Surjective.injective_comp_right`, `Surjective.right_cancellable`, no `comp_ne_zero_iff`/`comp_eq_zero_iff`), the group-action files (`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Action/Basic.lean` `MulAction.surjective`, `Pretransitive.lean` `MulAction.surjective_smul`, `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Pi/Basic.lean` `comp_ne_one_iff`), and `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/*` (`MulAction.IsPretransitive (GL (Fin 2) ℝ) ℍ`, `isPretransitiveGL2R`), plus Batteries and Lean core (no `comp_ne_zero`-style lemma). No Mathlib declaration states this result: at best it would need combining a library-specific surjectivity of `p • ·` (itself relying on `UpperHalfPlane.coe_heckeDiagMatrix_smul`, a library lemma) with a nonzero-composition principle that Mathlib does not provide as a single declaration, so neither `duplicate` nor a one-to-two-line `special_case` applies.
